summary:
EASD 2026 in Milan (Sep 28 – Oct 2) is driving a large wave of GLP-1 news, all within our channel focus.

**Top opportunity: EloraTZP.** Lilly's eloralintide + tirzepatide combination was announced today at 14:15 GMT. In a phase 2b trial of 367 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, the top dose averaged 23.3% weight loss vs 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg alone over 48 weeks. Mainstream coverage has only just started, and almost no creators have covered it yet.

**Retatrutide.** The TRIUMPH-2 paper is now published in The Lancet: 20.8% at the 12 mg dose vs 4.0% on placebo, over 80 weeks. Coverage is heavy (NBC, Time, SciAm, Guardian, CBS), so it is rising toward its peak. Our edge is the Lancet side-effect and dropout figures, plus a clear "not approved, don't buy it online" safety message.

**Company-funded comparisons.** Novo and Lilly released several of these at EASD:
- the oral Wegovy switch study (194 people, 4.1% at 3 months, no control group)
- orforglipron vs oral semaglutide (indirect comparison)
- Zepbound vs Wegovy HD (indirect comparison)
- semaglutide 2 mg vs switching to tirzepatide (HR 1.06)

Together they make a strong myth-busting explainer on how to read these studies. Any switching or dose topic stays at "ask your prescriber".

**The amylin wave.** Petrelintide (Lancet D&E), CagriSema and EloraTZP give us a timely "what is amylin?" explainer.

**Evergreen topics with fresh hooks:**
- hair loss (Guardian feature)
- Winter Arc (Oct 1): strength training and protein on GLP-1
- pancreatic cancer reassurance (two new datasets)
- the stopping-GLP-1 study in veterans

**Held to caution:** pregnancy (the French Diabetologia paper is unverified), counterfeit Ozempic, creatine for muscle loss (a commentary, not a trial), and the Novo-funded cardiovascular analysis.

**Rejected:** "stop insulin on GLP-1" (it's medication-change advice).

**Dropped:** the "heat wave" GLP-1 story. The ABC piece is from July and is off-season.

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide): top dose averaged 23.3% weight loss vs 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg alone at 48 weeks (phase 2b, 367 adults with obesity/overweight + type 2 diabetes, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Why add amylin to a GLP-1? Explain the 'second fullness hormone' in 45s: the top-dose number, the tirzepatide-alone comparator, more GI side effects, phase 2 only (phase 3 planned by end of 2026), not approved.
candidates.why_now: Announced today (30 Sep, 14:15 GMT) at EASD. Reuters, CNBC, STAT, MarketWatch and Endpoints covered it within minutes. MarketWatch's '23%' headline will go viral, but YouTube explainers are almost nonexistent.

evidence.signal: 23.3% (highest-dose combo) vs 14.8% tirzepatide 15 mg; A1C −2.9% vs −2.4%; 48 weeks; n=367
Advancing to phase 3
Mainstream pickup same day

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 published in The Lancet: 20.8% average weight loss on 12 mg vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks in adults with obesity + type 2 diabetes, with full side-effect and dropout data
candidates.angle: 'The Godzilla drug, with the fine print': the headline number next to placebo, how common diarrhea (27–34% vs 13%) and nausea (14–28% vs 8%) were, and how many people stopped because of side effects (up to 11.6% vs 4.9%). Also: it isn't approved, so anything sold online as retatrutide isn't Lilly's trial drug.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper and EASD presentation came out 29–30 Sep, and NBC, Time, SciAm, Guardian, CBS and the Independent are all covering it. Searches for 'retatrutide approval status' are showing up. We've tracked it for 3 snapshots with momentum rising (86 → 92).

evidence.signal: Phase 3 RCT published
Up to 20.8% in obesity with T2D; AE and discontinuation rates
12 mg: 20.8% (49.6 lb) at 80 weeks

candidates.topic: Amylin, the 'next GLP-1': petrelintide 10.7% vs 1.7% placebo at 42 weeks with GI tolerability similar to placebo (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, 493 adults)
candidates.angle: A pillar explainer: what amylin is, why it pairs with GLP-1, and where petrelintide, CagriSema and eloralintide each stand (as of Sept 2026). Show both estimands (10.7% efficacy, 10.2% treatment policy).
candidates.why_now: The Lancet D&E paper came out 29 Sep, the same week as EloraTZP and REIMAGINE 5 (CagriSema). 'Amylin' as a search term is set to rise as combo headlines spread.

evidence.signal: Lancet D&E publication + EASD data
Up to 10.7% vs 1.7% placebo, tolerability
Phase 2 RCT

candidates.topic: People who switched from GLP-1 injections to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide) lost 4.1% more on average after 3 months (OCTANE, 194 Ro telehealth patients, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Pill vs shot: what this study can and can't tell you.' It's a small, company-backed telehealth study with no control group, counting only people who stayed on treatment for 3 months. Useful questions to bring to your prescriber. No how-to-switch guidance.
keywords: switching from Wegovy injection to pill
candidates.why_now: Reuters, CNBC, Yahoo, KSL and Quartz ran it on 30 Sep. People already on injections are asking whether they can switch to the pill, a high-intent search.

evidence.signal: 4.1% (8.8 lb) at 3 months; about 2 in 5 reached ≥5%
Mainstream pickup; 194 patients, Ro platform

candidates.topic: The EASD 'GLP-1 wars': company-funded indirect comparisons (orforglipron 9.2% vs oral semaglutide 5.3% at 52 weeks; Zepbound vs Wegovy HD) and what 'indirect comparison' really means
candidates.angle: A myth-bust: 'No one tested these drugs side by side.' Explain indirect treatment comparisons, who funded each one, and why the headline gap (1.5–2.4 points) isn't a head-to-head trial result. Stay positive: both drug classes work, so talk to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Lilly and Novo both released competing analyses on 29–30 Sep (Reuters, Fierce, BioSpace). 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is always a high-volume search, and it just got fresh headlines.

evidence.signal: Foundayo 17.2 mg vs oral semaglutide 25 mg, indirect comparison (ACHIEVE-3 vs PIONEER PLUS)
Novo and Lilly pit their drugs against each other at EASD
Independent indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide (no T2D)

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide cause pancreatic cancer? Nordic regulator-mandated registry (97,464 matched pairs) plus a global propensity-matched cohort found no link
candidates.angle: A reassuring myth-bust with the real number in the title. Explain why registry studies were required, what 'no increased risk found' means, and which symptoms still need urgent care (severe tummy pain spreading to the back means call 911/999).
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots with momentum holding around 80. Medscape and News-Medical covered it 28–29 Sep, a J Pers Med cohort adds more data, and 'does tirzepatide cause cancer' is showing up as a query.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide not linked to higher pancreatic cancer risk
No increased risk of pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D, global matched cohort

candidates.topic: GLP-1 hair loss: how common it is, why it happens (telogen effluvium after rapid weight loss) and what supports regrowth
candidates.angle: A calm explainer. The shedding is usually temporary and tied to fast weight loss, not the drug 'attacking' hair. Cover what the evidence says about protein and nutrition (with the kidney caveat), and when to see a doctor. Name the one claims study with a 2.08× signal in women and note it's observational.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian ran a feature on 28 Sep, and supplement companies are pushing 'GLP-1 hair' products (Vollagen study). It's a high-volume, anxious search where evidence-based answers are scarce.

evidence.signal: 'Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?' feature
Hair loss with GLP-1 RA use, likely telogen effluvium

candidates.topic: 'Winter Arc' on a GLP-1: a 90-day strength training + protein plan to protect muscle while losing weight
candidates.angle: Ride the 1 Oct TikTok trend with a GLP-1 twist: the share of weight lost as lean mass in trials, then evidence-based resistance training and protein habits (with the kidney caveat). Encouraging tone, with no extreme dieting and no weight targets.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Zepbound
candidates.why_now: The Winter Arc challenge starts tomorrow (momentum 76–82 in earlier snapshots), and muscle-vs-fat is one of the playbook's double-down topics. Almost nobody has combined the two.

evidence.signal: Real-world 6-month tirzepatide body composition
Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss (commentary)

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to higher heart attack, stroke and death risk in 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes ('metabolic whiplash', observational)
candidates.angle: 'Why staying the course matters.' Explain what the study found (a link, not proof of cause), why cost and supply gaps push people to stop, and questions to raise with your prescriber before any change. No stopping or tapering advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots at 80–84. A Newswise piece today on costs lowering adherence adds a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Higher GLP-1 costs lead to lower adherence

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill: similar weight loss (up to ~14%) across pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women (ATTAIN-1/2 post-hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause blunt GLP-1 results?' A post-hoc analysis suggests not, for this pill. Frame it as encouraging for women 40–60, name the population, and note that post-hoc analyses have limits.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical ran it on 28 Sep. Menopause + GLP-1 is a huge search space for our 40–65 female audience, and few creators have covered this dataset.

evidence.signal: Uniform weight loss for women of all ages

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation, European Heart Journal) plus who lost the most weight (Diabetes Care)
candidates.angle: A differentiated explainer: 'It's not just the scale.' Cover the other ways GLP-1 may protect the heart (blood pressure, inflammation), with the exact SELECT population: adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight/obesity, without diabetes.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots, with momentum sliding from 74 to 58. Still useful as long-form or evergreen, but only with the 'beyond weight' angle.

evidence.signal: SELECT mediation analysis
Predictors of peak weight loss in SELECT

candidates.topic: GLP-1 kidney benefits beyond FLOW: SGLT2 + GLP-1 combined and renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes with and without albuminuria (BMJ target trial emulation)
candidates.angle: 'Your kidneys on GLP-1': FLOW trial basics (adults with T2D and CKD), then what new BMJ real-world data adds on kidney outcomes, including in people without albuminuria. Label it clearly as observational, and add 'ask about a kidney check (uACR)'.
candidates.why_now: The BMJ (16 Sep) and DOM (27 Sep) published new real-world data on adding a GLP-1 to SGLT2. The kidney pillar is under-covered by creators.

evidence.signal: Renal outcomes with SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA, target trial emulation
Adding GLP-1 RA to SGLT2i in CKD, population-based

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, another oral small-molecule GLP-1 pill, in a placebo-controlled RCT in early type 2 diabetes (Nature Medicine)
candidates.angle: 'The pill pipeline is filling up': a quick map of oral GLP-1s (oral semaglutide, orforglipron approved as Foundayo, safiglipron in trials), each with date-hedged status.
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on 29 Sep with almost no consumer coverage. It works best folded into a pipeline explainer.

evidence.signal: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial

candidates.topic: Semaglutide 2 mg escalation vs switching to tirzepatide: Novo-funded real-world analysis, MACE HR 1.06 (1.04–1.08) favoring semaglutide (COMPETE SWITCH CV, ~209,000 adults with T2D)
candidates.angle: Use only as a 'how to read a sponsored real-world study' case: a tiny difference, retrospective, manufacturer-funded, and Medical Daily's 'slightly lower'. Never frame it as 'raise your dose or switch'. Point people to their prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Covered by HCPLive, Benzinga, Cardiovascular Business and Clinical Trials Arena on 29–30 Sep. The topic sits close to dosing and switching advice, so handle with care.

evidence.signal: 2 mg escalation tied to lower MACE vs tirzepatide switch
Analyst comment on EASD data

candidates.topic: Fake Ozempic: two men charged with smuggling counterfeit semaglutide into the US. How to make sure your pen is genuine
candidates.angle: A protective, positive angle: get GLP-1s only with a prescription from a licensed pharmacy, check FDA counterfeit alerts, and know the warning signs of a fake pen. Never name or link any seller.
keywords: how to tell if Ozempic is real
candidates.why_now: pharmaphorum reported the charges on 30 Sep, and 'unapproved retatrutide' queries show gray-market interest spiking alongside the trial news.

evidence.signal: Two men charged with importing fake Ozempic

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and pregnancy in type 2 diabetes: new French nationwide study (Diabetologia) and meta-analyses find no increase in major birth defects
candidates.angle: Reassurance for people with T2D who become pregnant unexpectedly: what the data show, with evidence gaps stated. Always say to plan pregnancy with your clinician. No stopping or switching instructions.
candidates.why_now: The Diabetologia paper (29 Sep) and a Medical Xpress story (30 Sep) are out. The 'Ozempic babies' search interest persists. I couldn't confirm the French study's full details, so the fact-checker must verify.

evidence.signal: GLP-1s appear safe for diabetes in pregnancy, evidence gaps remain
French nationwide population-based study
Systematic review of GLP-1 RA exposure in pregnancy

candidates.topic: Creatine to protect muscle on GLP-1 medicines (Clinical Nutrition commentary)
candidates.angle: Only as part of a 'what's proven vs what's promising' muscle piece: resistance training and protein have the strongest evidence, while creatine alongside GLP-1s hasn't been tested in trials yet. No supplement promotion.
candidates.why_now: Clin Nutr published it on 21 Sep, and a Texas A&M creatine RCT is still trending. Supplement marketers will seize on it, so we get there first with a careful take.

evidence.signal: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss

candidates.topic: 'Can patients on GLP-1s stop taking insulin?' (Medscape)
candidates.angle: Not suitable: the topic is about stopping or changing prescribed medication. At most, a line saying 'any insulin change is a decision made with your clinician'.
candidates.why_now: Medscape ran it on 30 Sep, but covering it would break the 'no stopping or replacing medication' rule.

evidence.signal: Clinician-facing article on insulin deprescribing
